messages:
mira: FYI rolling an int4 per-channel variant of nimbus7b-lite to a small canary. early smoke looks ok but two things popped up: (1) a measurable rougeL drop on our news-summary evals, (2) sporadic OOMs on long-context microbatch=8 requests. tagging infra and ML. :wave:

kai: can you share the eval delta and a sample OOM trace? which kernel path did runtime select for the int4 build?

mira: quick paste: rougeL -2.1 vs fp16 on news-summary (stable promptset). p50/p95 latencies unchanged, p99 +12% on requests >1024 tokens. OOMs ~0.6% of canary sessions. runtime picked "sparse-attn-simd" with hybrid-kv prefetch. our canary config: ```
model: nimbus7b-lite
quant: int4_perchannel
kernel_policy: sparse-attn-simd
batching:
  microbatch: 8
  max_batch_ms: 12
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  prefetch_kv: true
```

ashley-sre: I grabbed the failing pod logs. core snippet: ```
2024-06-12T14:02:11Z ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
stack: runtime::alloc_buffer -> kv_cache::reserve -> attention::forward
ctx: seq_len=1536, total_batch_tokens=12288
```

leo-ml: that matches a class of issues we've seen: some int4 kernels tile/align buffers differently and hybrid prefetch + microbatching increases peak working set despite smaller model bytes. transient allocs for KV + tiling can spike.

mira: hypothesis: (A) prefetch_kv=true is warming big KV buffers per microbatch and combined with the siimd tiling causes spike; (B) quant calibration was small/unrepresentative leading to summary quality hit.

kai: proposed mitigations: 1) set defaults.max_new_tokens=128 for this variant, 2) flip prefetch_kv=false to avoid eager large allocations, 3) force kernel_policy to a less-aggressive path e.g. "dense-fast" for a/b, 4) redo calibration with larger, stratified dataset and per-layer clipping.

mira: I'll prepare a canary patch toggling (1)-(3) and run the bigger calibration job in parallel. rollout plan: 10% -> 24h metrics -> if OOMs <0.1% and rouge delta <0.5 then 50%.

tess-prod: product comment: auto-fallback to int8 for long sessions would reduce user-visible regressions. can we add a routing rule?

mira: yes, adding route rule: if seq_len>1024 && variant==int4 -> route to int8 variant. also adding a canary rollback hook if p99 latency or quality regressions spike.

ashley-sre: infra actions: pin kernel affinity for canary hosts to avoid noisy neighbor kernel changes, add a soft cgroup threshold to catch big allocs and return 429 instead of killing the node. opening ticket INFRA-6412.

leo-ml: for the quality side: we'll re-run quantization with 5k calibration samples across news/docs/code, use per-layer MSE clipping, and add a logits-distance metric (topk L2) against fp16 to catch distributional shift. also try symmetric vs asymmetric scales for problematic layers.

kai: also consider reducing microbatch from 8->4 for long-seq serving to smooth transient peaks; we lose batching efficiency but avoid OOMs. can measure token cost impact in the optimizer.

mira: starting canary patch: set max_new_tokens=128, prefetch_kv=false, kernel_policy=dense-fast, microbatch remains 8 for baseline A; B variant will be microbatch=4. pushing to 10% now.

dev-bot: canary-patch PR #4127 created by mira -> queued for rollout.

mira: I'll post eval sweep results and canary metrics here in ~4-6 hours. if we still see quality drop after re-calibration we'll snapshot examples and run a focused ablation per-layer. thanks all. :thumbsup:
